content:
I'll fully admit that my DIY iPhone camera modification looks pretty ridiculous — but it genuinely makes my iPhone more practical and more enjoyable to shoot with.

It started as a solution to a specific video shoot scenario, but unexpectedly I've found myself using it over and over again...

In the world of compact cameras, one of the biggest divides has been whether or not to include a viewfinder. Historically, enthusiasts have argued strongly for electronic viewfinders (EVF) over optical ones, but EVFs are now so good that almost no one cares anymore.

But whether optical or electronic, the viewfinder offers a very practical advantage over using the rear screen to compose, especially when shooting in bright sunlight. Even with the screen brightness maxed out, when the sun is fierce, it's still very difficult to see what you're shooting, and you may also have to deal with screen glare.

While it hasn't historically been a huge issue in London, this summer has brought record-breaking heatwaves, and honestly, I feel like the last time I saw a cloud or rain was about thirty years ago.

To me, though, there's more to it than just that. I also feel there's a psychological difference between only seeing what's in the frame and seeing the surrounding context while shooting. Sometimes, that's exactly the main reason I use a dedicated camera instead of a phone.

When I was choosing a camera for video a few years ago, the Blackmagic Pocket Cinema Camera 4K was clearly the hot choice, but the lack of a viewfinder gave me pause. In the end I figured it wasn't a big deal for me, since I'd mainly be using it indoors, and when I needed to use it outdoors, adding a large screen with a sun hood would solve most of the problems.

However, sometimes I want to operate in a more compact form than the full setup with the screen added, so I found a simple accessory suited for outdoor use. It's a combination sun hood and magnifying loupe that magnetically attaches to the camera's rear screen, effectively providing an optical viewfinder.

I was about to have a shoot where I'd be using both the BMPCC 4K and the iPhone 16 Pro Max for video. I went to the location and did a quick test, and found the viewfinder accessory really useful. Since the BMPCC 4K and iPhone have very similar screen sizes, I wondered if I could use it on the iPhone.

Of course the iPhone doesn't have magnetic attachment, but the iPhone is light enough that holding it against the loupe with my hand is not a problem at all. I was pleasantly surprised at how well it worked, especially when I was using the camera control button as a shutter.

Since then I've used this accessory in quite a few shooting situations, and whether it's being able to see the screen more clearly in harsh sunlight or just the feeling of immersion, it's made the experience more enjoyable. My iPhone became my go-to camera a long time ago, and with this DIY modification, I feel like there will be even more situations where the phone is the only camera I need.

A ridiculous or genius creation? Let me know what you think in the comments. If you think it's the latter, I'm sorry to say the product I bought seems to have been discontinued, and I haven't yet seen anything similar designed for screens larger than three inches. If you find one, please post a link in the comments.
